title: check all reports all options passed while never naming the options that did not activate, so a narrowed run is indistinguishable from a full one
body:
Found by `utilz/cc` on 2026-09-09, who measured it in their tree BEFORE fixing their config, on the grounds that after the fix it is unobservable. **Reproduced here in devbin's own tree, which is the estate that ships the runner.**

    $ out="$(bin/devbin check all 2>&1)"; rc=$?
    rc=0
    ran:     syntax lint critic format toolchain
    absent:  compile deps clippy autotests targetdir
    tail:    all check options passed

`lib/builtins` catalogues EIGHT `check` options -- `compile`(elixir) `deps`(elixir) `clippy`(rust) `autotests`(rust) `targetdir`(rust) `format`(any) `toolchain`(any) `critic`(any). Devbin declares only `shell`, so the five language-scoped ones never activate. **They appear nowhere in the output: not run, not listed, not skipped, not named.** The tail then speaks for the survivors, and `all check options passed` at rc 0 is indistinguishable to a reader from a full pass.

**THE DISCRIMINATOR IS NOT WHETHER DEVBIN REPORTS NARROWING -- IT IS WHERE THE NARROWING HAPPENS**, and both behaviours sit side by side in one run:

- `check format` RAN and announced its own narrowing: `no formattable language declared -- nothing to check`. Correct, legible, exactly right.
- `check toolchain` did the same: `no .tool-versions -- this project declares no toolchain pin`.
- The five language-scoped gates were never INSTANTIATED, so nothing could announce anything, and the aggregate counted only what spoke.

A gate that runs and finds nothing has a voice. A gate that never activates does not.

**MECHANISM.** `run_all` iterates `$(command_options "$cmd")`, which is the ACTIVE set. Its `skipped` variable is assigned in exactly one place -- inside the `in_all: false` branch -- so it structurally cannot carry an option that was deactivated by language scope or by `enabled: false`. Those options are gone before the loop, and nothing downstream knows they existed.

**THIS IS THE FIFTH ENTRANCE TO A CLASS `run_all` ALREADY CLOSES FROM FOUR SIDES, and its own comments are the argument for fixing it.** That function refuses a verdict on zero options ("success reported for having done nothing, which is the exact false green the sealed gates exist to prevent"), refuses on zero EXECUTED after `in_all` exclusions ("a run that examined nothing is not a pass"), reports `skipped (in_all: false)` because "a run that quietly skipped half its gates and printed 'all passed' is a false green", and refuses when a return code and its seal disagree. **Every one of those is this defect approached from a different direction. The inactive-option door is the one still open**, and it is the widest, because language scoping is the ordinary case rather than a misconfiguration.

**NOT A DUPLICATE OF 0062 AND IT SURVIVES 0062's FIX.** 0062 is the two-file language split. This is that the aggregate verdict is silent about any option that did not instantiate, for ANY reason -- language scope, `enabled: false`, or a source not yet invented. Fixing 0062 would have made Utilz's rust gates activate and left every elixir gate in every shell project just as invisible.

**Suggested shape, not a ruling.** The runner already has the vocabulary: `skipped (in_all: false)` is the right sentence one case over. What is missing is an INACTIVE line naming the catalogued options that did not instantiate and why, printed on every path including the passing one, so the summary's reach is visible beside its verdict. `check critic` in this same run already models the standard: *"2 of 6 rule(s) ASKED of this run; 2 armed in total. A clean result covers what was ASKED and says nothing about the rest."* That sentence is what the aggregate needs and lacks.

Severity high rather than critical only because the narrowing is deterministic from declared languages and an operator could in principle derive it. Nothing in the output invites them to.

---

## Amended 2026-09-09 -- the fix shape, corrected twice by `utilz/cc` and once by measurement

**A PARTITION CONTROL BEATS THE LISTING, AND IT IS THEIRS.** Assert that `ran + skipped(in_all) + inactive == candidates` and REFUSE when the parts do not sum. Four of the five doors above were closed by naming a specific failure; a remainder that must sum closes the DOORWAY, including directions nobody has thought of -- a future filter that removes options before the loop breaks the arithmetic whether or not anyone remembered to give it a voice. Their formulation of why: too WIDE fails loudly, too NARROW fails greenly, and only a remainder that must sum catches the narrow direction. This function already refuses on zero options and on zero executed; a partition check is the same instinct one step up.

**AND DO NOT ENUMERATE ON EVERY RUN.** Reciting five inactive options in a single-language project is noise, and a gate that is noisy in the ordinary case is one people learn to skim -- which is how the loud half of this class turns back into the quiet half. `check critic` in the same output already models the right shape: *"2 of 6 rule(s) ASKED of this run; 2 armed in total."* State the denominator without reciting the members -- `5 of 8 options ran; 3 inactive (languages not declared)` -- and expand names only on request or on refusal.

**THE DENOMINATOR IS NOT `lib/builtins`, AND A CONTROL THAT READS IT FLAT WOULD GO RED IN THE ORDINARY CASE.** Measured rather than assumed. `command_options` builds its candidate set as the deduplicated UNION of `cfg_list "commands.$cmd.options"` and `builtin_options "$cmd"`, then filters by `option_active`. Two consequences the sum control must honour:

- `builtin_options` returns EMPTY when a project handler displaces the built-in set, so in any estate owning its own `check` handler the catalogue contributes nothing. A partition asserted against the flat eight would refuse every such run. **That is the "a gate red in the ordinary case is how a gate teaches people to ignore it" failure, one level up from where this codebase already records it.**
- The union is deduplicated, so an option both config-declared and catalogued is one candidate. Counting the sources separately over-counts and refuses on a correct run.

Devbin's own run is the worked example: five ran, of which `syntax` and `lint` are config-declared and not in the catalogue at all, so `ran(5) + catalogued(8)` is not an arithmetic anyone should be doing.

**THE INFORMATION ALREADY EXISTS AND IS DISCARDED ON THE WAY OUT, WHICH MAKES THIS CHEAPER THAN IT LOOKS.** `command_options` computes the candidate set and the active set four lines apart, and its `seen` variable already holds every candidate. The inactive set is exactly `seen` minus what was printed. Nothing new has to be derived -- a second channel has to be kept rather than dropped. **`run_all` is the wrong home for the arithmetic because by the time it runs it can only see survivors**, which is the whole defect restated as an architectural fact.

**Credit, stated because an issue read later gets it wrong otherwise.** `utilz/cc` ran the gate, reported a refusal they could not explain, and -- because the population question reached them before their repair did -- measured `check all` on the unfixed tree, which is the measurement that makes this reportable at all. The partition control and the do-not-enumerate warning are both theirs. The two-file diagnosis and the reproduction in devbin's own tree are mine.


---

## Fixed 2026-09-16 -- the partition, built from cc's design (vc), reviewed by dc

**Commits:** `893344b` (the fix) and `4de32f6` (the arm dc's review asked for).

`command_option_candidates` is now the one enumeration: the deduplicated union of `commands.<cmd>.options` and `builtin_options`. `command_options` filters it by `option_active`. `run_all` takes the offered set before anything is filtered, and asks `option_active` of EACH candidate for the inactive set, never deriving it from `command_options`. It then prints one count line on every path: pass, fail, and the zero-options refusal. devbin's own `check all` now reads:

    5 of 10 check options ran; 5 inactive here (bin/devbin help --why names them), 0 skipped (in_all: false)

`option_partition_gap` is pure. When every candidate is ran, skipped or inactive exactly once, it prints nothing. Otherwise it names what is `unaccounted for`, `not an option here` or `counted twice`, and `run_all` REFUSES A VERDICT: rc 1, the pass line suppressed, and every part listed. Members are named only on refusal. The line points at `help --why`, which already names each inactive option with its reason.

**Arms, in `tests/unit/dispatch.bats`:**

- the passing count, with `enabled: false` and `in_all: false`;
- a fully active run;
- `test` in a project declaring no languages, with the count read from the fixture's catalogue;
- a project handler, whose denominator is config-only;
- an option both config-declared and catalogued, counted once and run once;
- a stub appended to the fixture's vendored `lib/resolve` that drops an active option;
- a stub that repeats options;
- the pure not-an-option-here walk.

**Mutation checks.** vc's nine were all killed; candidate dedupe survived at first, and the overlap arm was added to kill it. dc's review ran three more: dropping the catalogue from the candidates and double-recording an `in_all: false` option were killed, while deleting the not-an-option-here walk survived. The pure arm now kills that one. The suite is 1145/1145 at `893344b`, in a detached worktree.

**Residual, agreed with dc.** The candidate set is read from `cfg_list` and `builtin_options` inside a heredoc. A failure there would narrow the denominator, and the partition could not see it. It is unreachable from today's static catalogue, and the zero-options and overlap arms go red if the catalogue drops out wholesale.

**cc's `||`-fallback question, deferred here, is ruled a separate class.** 0063 narrows the population before counting, and its cure is a partition that must sum. The `||` form lets one exit status stand for two outcomes, and its cure is to tell them apart. It is in `intent/llm/LESSONS.md` at `16ebacb`.
